sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct used for expression and characterization; specific surface-expression or functional assay results are not detailed in the ledger clip.
sites.rationale: CLMP is a type-I single-pass transmembrane protein; its signal peptide (residues 1–18) is cleaved co-translationally, leaving residue 19 (T) as the mature extracellular N-terminus. Because the paper states the HA tag was added to the 'N-terminus' of the full-length protein without specifying a residue, and because there is exactly one extracellular N-terminal position (the junction between the cleaved SP and the mature ectodomain), the position is topology-derived at insert_after_residue = 18. Python verification confirms residue 18 = G and residue 19 = T, consistent with the numbered sequence. The tag site is 215 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 234), well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. Full-length human CLMP (aa 1–373) was N-terminally HA-tagged (HA-Clmp) and expressed in pGW1 for expression and characterization studies. The paper names only 'N-terminus' with no residue number. CLMP has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–18; a tag placed upstream of residue 19 would be co-translationally cleaved with the signal peptide and lost. The sole viable extracellular N-terminal junction is therefore after residue 18 (last SP residue, G) and before residue 19 (T, mature N-terminus), placing the HA tag on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: For HA-Clmp, the HA epitope was added to the N-terminus of human Clmp in pGW1.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It reports an HA tag at the N-terminus of full-length human CLMP (aa 1–373). No residue number is given, but the signal peptide (residues 1–18) constrains the only viable extracellular N-terminal junction to after residue 18. No internal extracellular loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or intracellular tags are reported in the ledger. The large extracellular domain (residues 19–233, ~215 aa) contains two Ig-like domains typical of CAR-family proteins, but no ledger evidence supports any internal loop insertion for CLMP specifically, so no internal sites are proposed.
